metadata.title: HDBLAST: Registered Causal Scalar Response and Independent Forced-Mode Calibration
metadata.description:
This prospective fixed-geometry experiment calibrates the renormalized retarded scalar variance response at the minimal Euclidean/Bunch-Davies de Sitter reference x0=r=2H². Two smooth compact external pulses, six observation times and three finite momentum cutoffs were published with implementation and gate hashes before execution. Independent forced canonical modes agree with the matched finite-cutoff and time-memory calculations. The dataset includes raw mode arrays, all 36 comparisons, 17 wrong-formula/state checks, 46 exact symbolic identities and 14 symbolic controls, with normal and optimized validation.

Directed interval arithmetic encloses the actual combined omitted-momentum tail. Quadrature, arithmetic and mode-refinement errors retain distinct empirical estimates and acceptance rules; the complete response is not a certified interval solution. The analytic spectral-work companion separates positive canonical excitation energy from reference-dependent background drift and physical minimal-stress polarization; no energy yield is computed.

The finite-part causal kernel is an established method, not a novelty claim. This result supplies only one fixed-reference scalar susceptibility. Matched stress and metric kernels, actual stationary-endpoint response, bulk conditions and quantum initial data remain required before coupled evolution or quantum stability. No heating, thermalization, cosmological observation or Big-Bang origin is established. AI-assisted reviews are internal cross-checks rather than external peer review. The numerical package includes the required local protocol inputs and can be replayed independently of private research folders on the pinned Linux environment. Text, figures and data use CC BY 4.0; source code uses MIT. Prepared metadata does not attest to a completed deposit or DOI.
